body:
Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure. Detects failures across transport, water, energy, communications, and buildings and coordinates repairs.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 82 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Megastructures and Planetary Transformation". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Predictive maintenance is deployed (rail, aviation, grids); global cross-sector self-maintenance is unproven.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Detects failures across transport, water, energy, communications, and buildings and coordinates repairs.
body:
Known science foundations of Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure.

Airlines predict engine failures; railways monitor tracks; utilities predict transformer faults. Structural health monitoring covers bridges. Smart-grid self-healing reroutes power. Coordinating repairs across all infrastructure sectors as one system is the unsolved integration.

Key quantity check (US infrastructure grade (ASCE) as GPA / grade needed for self-maintenance): computed ratio 0.5 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.2. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Detects failures across transport, water, energy, communications, and buildings and coordinates repairs.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure.

Sensors do not cover most infrastructure. Repair still needs human crews and parts. Cross-sector coordination lacks authority and protocols.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 6.5 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is unmonitored assets vs prediction lead time at 6.5 orders of magnitude (unmonitored assets larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: Detects failures across transport, water, energy, communications, and buildings and coordinates repairs.
body:
Unresolved problems for Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure, in priority order (research burden index 19, 1 blocking):

Automated repair (not just detection) (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Cross-sector authority (severity 2/3, tractability 1/3; priority 6).

Sensor coverage gaps (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

What would count as evidence of success for Self-Maintaining Global Infrastructure:

Predicts a failure with 30-day lead (weight 0.4; SATISFIED).

Self-heals a grid fault automatically (weight 0.35; SATISFIED).

Coordinates cross-sector repairs (weight 0.25; not yet satisfied).

Evidence confidence: 0.75 (2 of 3 criteria satisfied). Verdict: strong. Confidence here measures satisfied evidence, not belief.
